headline: Granted a special permit for dog training and pet sitting at 43 King Street; $750,000 and $291,912.91 transfers went to committee.
summary: A $75,000 Mass Gaming Commission grant for lighting in the Puerto Rican Cultural District was adopted on a 10-1 vote. State funds of $352,020.27 for the snow and ice deficit were also accepted. The Clean Slate resolution and six Historical Commission appointments went to committee.
decisions: Laid on the table the June 11, 2024, September 4, 2024, and April 15, 2025 executive session minutes.
Laid on the table the December 9, 2024 Finance Committee executive session minutes.
Received and adopted the minutes from September 2, 2026.
Laid on the table an order to elect a treasurer at the April 21, 2026 meeting, combining the Treasurer and Collector positions.
Referred six Historical Commission appointments by Mayor Joshua Garcia to the Public Service Committee.
Received the Holyoke Conservation Commission minutes from May 14, 2026.
Received the Board of Fire Commission minutes from August 19, 2026.
Approved $462.55 from the DPW City Hall account for unpaid fiscal 2026 bills, 11-0.
Accepted the $352,020.27 FY2026 WRAP allocation from MassDOT for the snow and ice deficit, 11-0.
Accepted the $10,000.00 Massachusetts Health Officers Association stipend, 11-0.
Accepted the $8,550.00 MEMA grant with no match, 11-0.
Accepted the $75,000.00 FY2027 Mass Gaming Commission community mitigation grant for lighting in the Puerto Rican Cultural District, 10-1.
Granted a special permit for a dog training and pet sitting business at 43 King Street, with conditions on signs, dogs, and hours, 10-1.
Referred the barber shop special permit at 113 Sargeant Street back to committee.
Referred a request to invite the Registrar and Board of Voters to discuss voter participation.

Approved an order asking the Law Department for an opinion on a data center ban or a moratorium.

Referred a $750,000.00 transfer from Cannabis Stabilization to Ezekiel’s Plan 2.0 to the Finance Committee.
Referred a request to consider teacher PD days on election days when schools are polling places to the Joint City Council and School Committee.
Referred the Clean Slate resolution to the Development and Governmental Relations Committee.
Referred a $291,912.91 transfer from Cannabis Stabilization to Claims-General to the Finance Committee.

1 
 
REGULAR MEETING OF THE CITY COUNCIL 
September 15, 2026 
The meeting was called to order by President Murphy-Romboletti at 6:39 p.m.  
The Clerk called the roll.  Absent Members: 2 (I. Rivera, J. Rivera) Present Members in person: 11 
(Anderson-Burgos, Devine, Greaney, Magrath-Smith, Maisonet, Murphy-Romboletti, Panitch, Purcell, 
Sullivan, Thalheimer, Vacon).  
The Pledge of Allegiance was recited. 
President Murphy-Romboletti asked for a moment of silence in honor of the passing of Councilor Jenny 
Rivera’s father, Juan Jusino, and to keep Jenny and her family in everyone’s thoughts.  
A moment of silence was recognized for Mr. Jusino.  
President Murphy-Romboletti noted that there were many people in attendance for a special recognition. 
She then called up Councilor Thalheimer to present a proclamation.  
Councilor Thalheimer invited Jimmy Camacho into chambers and to the podium. She then stated that Mr. 
Camacho’s incredible work helped to elevate Holyoke, the sport of volleyball, and the island of Puerto 
Rico simultaneously. She then presented a City Council proclamation as well as a citation from Mayor 
Garcia recognizing Mr. Camacho’s work to document the history of volleyball in Holyoke and its 
connections to Puerto Rican culture, helping to organize a Puerto Rico volleyball exhibit at the 
International Volleyball Hall of Fame. She added that his research yielded a display that celebrated the 
history, achievements, and cultural impact of volleyball throughout Puerto Rico.  
J. Camacho thanked Edgar Padilla, a point guard from UMass and personal friend, for helping to give him 
access to everyone in Puerto Rico and creating a lot of meetings. He also thanked Jorge Jimenez who 
provided a lot of memorabilia. He also thanked Michelle and Richard Duff, niece and nephew of the late 
Ricky Amon, the first Puerto Rican enshrined at the Hall of Fame, for their input and access include Mr. 
Amon in the exhibit, emphasizing the importance of handling his memory appropriately. He added that 
Mr. Amon was a perfect figure as a Puerto Rican of Irish descent. He also thanked Pedro Rodríguez and 
President Rafúl Rodrígues, President and Vice President of the Puerto Rican Volleyball Hall of Fame for 
giving him items for the exhibit. He also thanked Edmundo Jimenez, his roommate at UMass. He also 
thanked others who had been there as support both in Puerto Rico and Holyoke, including Mayor Joshua 
Garcia, George Mulry, Executive Director of the Volleyball Hall of Fame, Aaron Vega for helping allocate 
$10,000 for the exhibit, Gabriel Rosario for his artwork at the exhibit, Manuel Frau for giving him access 
to Gabriel, Cesar Ruiz, Emo Morales, Gregner Gotay for giving him access to players, as well as Theresa 
Cooper-Gordon, Juan Mantano, and many others who provided access and support. He also thanked 
people for their patience, recognizing that he probably got a lot of people’s nerves working on this. He 
also recognized President Murphy-Romboletti for the hard work she puts in.  
The name of Councilor Greaney was pulled to head the roll call voting. 
PRESIDENT'S REPORT
2 
 
President Murphy-Romboletti stated that a free movie night for seniors would be held at Pulaski Park on 
September 19th at 7 p.m. where they would be playing Thelma.  
She also stated that the IVHF induction ceremony would be on Saturday, October 17th.  
She then stated that Holyoke Day at the Big E would be on September 22nd. She then stated that the 
administrative assistant would ensure councilors attending would receive details.  
Councilor Devine asked about the IVHF event, noting that she believed it was 6-8 p.m. on the 16th. 
President Murphy-Romboletti clarified that was the date of the Mayor’s Reception event.  
 
PUBLIC HEARING  
PUBLIC COMMENT 
(20:20) 
David Owen, 12 Mason Road, noted that Mayor Garcia had recently correctly stated that the city had 
much to be proud of, including the Volleyball Hall of Fame, the Holyoke Taxpayers Association, the 
Veterans Hall of fame, Wistariahurst, among several local parks, infrastructure, and other great 
institutions and organizations. He then noted that there was recent discussion of state income tax drawing 
statements of interest and uncertainty and jeopardizing reversing some of the city’s progress. He then 
suggested that pride in Holyoke didn’t need to be at the behest of Boston. He then suggested that value 
would come from more local fiscal responsibility, accountability, and public transparency.  
Christian Carde Guzman, 203 West Franklin, expressed support for the Clean Slate resolution and the 
TOPA resolution featured in item 29, emphasizing that both spoke to many of the challenges people in 
Holyoke faced every day. He then stated that Clean Slate would help people who had completed 
sentences move forward with their lives to find stable jobs and housing without a record following them for 
several years. He added that TOPA was also important, emphasizing how difficult rising housing costs 
were to helping people stay in their neighborhoods. He added that TOPA would give tenants first 
opportunity to buy their buildings if they are put up for sale. He then asked the Council to support both 
resolutions.  
Jeannette Rivera, spoke on behalf of Ashley Morales from Ward 2, expressing support for item 29, 
specifically the resolution supporting automatic record sealing, emphasizing that past mistakes should not 
impact someone’s ability to be able to move forward. She added that Ms. Morales’ family of 4 
experienced a lot of hardship because he husband struggled to find employment due to his record until he 
was able to find a second chance working for Wayfinders.  
Caitlyn Moran, Ward 5, spoke in favor of the resolutions in item 29, Clean Slate as well as The 
Opportunity to Purchase Act (TOPA). She then stated that she believed in making life better for everyone, 
especially for those who were marginalized. She expressed further concern for those who were charged 
while they were minors that should not have their entire lives affected by mistakes when they were kids 
but tried as adults. She added that everyone should have a chance for safe, stable, and affordable 
housing, and tenants should have the right of first refusal to purchase their buildings and avoid risking 
their buildings being purchased by corporate landlords that will jack up their rents.
3 
 
REGULAR AND PENDING EXECUTIVE SESSION MINUTES  
(29:05)

4. Vacon, Greaney- ORDER: that city council go to the first ballot to elect a treasurer at the April 21, 2026 
city council meeting in accordance with our current charter.  Our city council appointed Collector has 
indicated interest in the Treasurer/Collector position.  A majority of the city council has had the 
opportunity to interview our Collector. This appointment would legally establish the Treasurer position & 
for practical purposes combines the positions, while waiting for further charter changes that will be sent to 
the state legislature in a home rule petition.  Transition changes can happen in coordination with other 
ordinance changes. 
--->  Laid on the table.

(29:55)

package.

4

--->  Received and referred to the Public Service Committee.

10. From Mayor Joshua Garcia-letter appointing Ms. Fleur Kuhta of 124 Chestnut St. to serve on the new

Councilor Devine questioned if items 7 and 8 needed to be sent to committee, noting they had been

President Murphy-Romboletti suggested that as this would be a new commission, everyone should be

--->  Received and referred to the Public Service Committee.

--->  Received. 
12. From Board of Fire Commission-meeting minutes from August 19, 2026. 
--->  Received. 
PETITIONS 
REPORTS OF COMMITTEES 
(32:25) 
13. The Committee on Finance to whom was referred an order that the amount of FOUR HUNDRED

HALL (14222-52502) appropriation in fiscal year 2027 for goods/services received in fiscal year 2026 
which were unencumbered at the 2026 fiscal year end. 
have considered the same and Recommended that the order be adopted.

Patricia Devine 
Michael Sullivan 
Meg Magrath-Smith
5

Nicole Maisonet

unencumbered. 
--->  Report of Committee passed two readings and Adopted on a call of the roll of the yeas and nays--
Yeas  11--Nays  0--Absent  2 (I. Rivera, J. Rivera).

$352,020.27 FY2026 WRAP formula allocation from the Massachusetts Department of Transportation 
and authorizes its use and accounting in accordance with applicable MassDOT requirements and DLS 
Bulletin BUL-2026-04, including use of the special revenue fund treatment for WRAP reimbursements 
applied to the City’s FY2026 snow and ice deficit. 
have considered the same and Recommended that the order be adopted. 
Committee Members: 
     
Patricia Devine 
Michael Sullivan 
Meg Magrath-Smith 
Juan Anderson-Burgos 
Nicole Maisonet 
UNDER DISCUSSION: 
Councilor Devine stated that this was from the state offering funds to cities and towns to cover snow 
related deficit spending. She noted that this may not cover the entire deficit the city had.  
--->  Report of Committee passed two readings and Adopted on a call of the roll of the yeas and nays--
Yeas  11--Nays  0--Absent  2 (I. Rivera, J. Rivera). 
15. The Committee on Finance to whom was referred an order that in accordance with M.G.L. Chapter 44 
Sec. 53A, the City Council hereby accepts the provisions of the “MASSACHUSETTS HEALTH 
OFFICERS ASSOCIATION, $10,000.00”, stipend and authorizes the establishment of a Fund or other 
method appropriate for the accounting of the receipts and expenditures of all resources associated with 
the administration of said stipend. 
Sec 2-509 - Grant Reporting 
Any city department, of which has received grant funding by approval of the city council pursuant to 
Massachusetts General Laws, or any other authorizing criteria, shall within a reasonable period of time, 
but no later than 60 days from the conclusion of said grant, generate a detailed report which outlines the 
planned outcomes with the documented actual results. Said report shall be submitted to the city clerk for 
addition to the city council's next agenda. 
have considered the same and Recommended that the order be adopted. 
Committee Members: 
     
Patricia Devine 
Michael Sullivan
6 
 
Meg Magrath-Smith 
Juan Anderson-Burgos 
Nicole Maisonet 
UNDER DISCUSSION: 
Councilor Devine stated that the grant was for the Board of Health and was used as reimbursement for 
training an intern. She added that the intern did so well that they were hired into the department. She 
added that the remaining funds would be used to subscribe to a Board of Health related lawyer group the 
BOH sought advice from.  
--->  Report of Committee passed two readings and Adopted on a call of the roll of the yeas and nays--
Yeas  11--Nays  0--Absent  2 (I. Rivera, J. Rivera). 
16. The Committee on Finance to whom was referred an order that in accordance with M.G.L. Chapter 44 
Sec. 53A, the City Council hereby accepts the provisions of the “MASSACHUSETTS EMERGENCY 
MANAGEMENT AGENCY (MEMA), $8,550.00, NO MATCH” grant, and authorizes the establishment of a 
Fund or other method appropriate for the accounting of the receipts and expenditures of all resources 
associated with the administration of said grant. 
Sec 2-509 - Grant Reporting 
Any city department, of which has received grant funding by approval of the city council pursuant to 
Massachusetts General Laws, or any other authorizing criteria, shall within a reasonable period of time, 
but no later than 60 days from the conclusion of said grant, generate a detailed report which outlines the 
planned outcomes with the documented actual results. Said report shall be submitted to the city clerk for 
addition to the city council's next agenda. 
have considered the same and Recommended that the order be adopted. 
Committee Members: 
     
Patricia Devine 
Michael Sullivan 
Meg Magrath-Smith 
Juan Anderson-Burgos 
Nicole Maisonet 
UNDER DISCUSSION: 
Councilor Devine stated that the grant would be used for the Emergency Management Department to 
update furniture in their operations center. She added that there would be an in kind match for the grant. 
--->  Report of Committee passed two readings and Adopted on a call of the roll of the yeas and nays--
Yeas  11--Nays  0--Absent  2 (I. Rivera, J. Rivera). 
17. The Committee on Finance to whom was referred an order that in accordance with M.G.L. Chapter 44 
Sec. 53A, the City Council hereby accepts the provisions of the “FY2027 MASS GAMING COMMISSION 
COMMUNITY MITIGATION, $75,000.00, NO MATCH” grant, and authorizes the establishment of a Fund 
or other method appropriate for the accounting of the receipts and expenditures of all resources 
associated with the administration of said grant. 
Sec 2-509 - Grant Reporting 
Any city department, of which has received grant funding by approval of the city council pursuant to 
Massachusetts General Laws, or any other authorizing criteria, shall within a reasonable period of time, 
but no later than 60 days from the conclusion of said grant, generate a detailed report which outlines the
7 
 
planned outcomes with the documented actual results. Said report shall be submitted to the city clerk for 
addition to the city council's next agenda. 
have considered the same and Recommended that the order be adopted. 
Committee Members: 
     
Patricia Devine 
Michael Sullivan 
Meg Magrath-Smith 
Juan Anderson-Burgos 
Nicole Maisonet 
UNDER DISCUSSION: 
Councilor Devine stated that Holyoke was eligible to receive this money from the Mass Gaming 
Commission. She then explained that this would be used to improve lighting in the Puerto Rican Cultural 
District. She noted that Councilor Sullivan brought up concerns with the electric bills, and the explanation 
was that they would watch the electric bills to make sure they didn’t get too high. She also stated that the 
funds from this grant had decreased over the years, noting that the amount had been over $200,000 in 
previous years but was now only $75,000. She added that some of the funds in the past were used for 
murals.  
Councilor Sullivan stated that while he voted for this in committee, he was now questioning the funds 
being used on more murals and lighting with all of the other problems the city had, particularly incidents 
on High Street that were affecting the vibrancy of the city. He added that there were better used for it.  
Councilor Thalheimer emphasized that lighting was a public safety preventative measure. She added that 
murals brought vibrance and cultural relevance to the city.  
Councilor Anderson-Burgos agreed with those sentiments, adding that a mural that had its reveal the past 
Saturday was one he had been working to bring to the city for years. He emphasized that the mural would 
not have happened without this grant, adding that it represented the community’s heart. He added that 
Commonwealth Murals was the community doing stuff for the community. He further emphasized that 
murals brightened the city and were inspirational.  
Councilor Purcell stated that murals were also an economic driver that help improve tourism in the city.  
Councilor Greaney asked to move the question.  
Councilor Devine congratulated Councilor Anderson-Burgos for his work bringing a mural to the city 
featuring the first Puerto Rican superhero. 
--->  Report of Committee passed two readings and Adopted on a call of the roll of the yeas and nays--
Yeas  10--Nays  1 (Sullivan)--Absent  2 (I. Rivera, J. Rivera). 
(46:40) 
President Murphy-Romboletti stated that items 18 and 19 remained in committee.
8 
 
20. The Committee on Development and Governmental Relations to whom was referred a Special permit 
application for home occupation of John Barbagallo for a dog training and pet sitting business at 43 King 
Street (123-00-061) per 4.8.2. 
have considered the same and Recommended that the special permit be granted with the following 
conditions: 
1. That there shall be no signage; 
2. That there shall be no more than 2 dogs on site at a time; 
3. That there be no drop-offs prior to 7 a.m. and no pickups after 7 p.m. 
Committee Members: 
     
Richard P. Purcell 
Michael Sullivan 
Mimi Panitch 
Nicole Maisonet 
Israel Rivera 
UNDER DISCUSSION: 
Councilor Purcell stated that this was Mr. Barbagallo’s primary occupation. He then noted that there was 
lively discussion on this, which included statement from 3 citizens who disagreed with the permit. He then 
explained that the concerns included issues about zoning and noise, and Mr. Barbagallo addressed those 
concerns to the committee’s satisfaction. He added that another concern was that this would be a kennel, 
and it was clarified that this would not be a kennel. He added that the primary job would be pet sitting but 
that there would be training as well. 
Councilor Greaney asked if the training sessions would be indoors, outdoors, or both.  
Councilor Purcell stated that it would be both, including teaching dogs how to handle being on a leash. He 
added that Mr. Barbagallo was fully insured.  
Councilor Greaney expressed concern that it would involve the whole neighborhood. 
Councilor Purcell stated that Mr. Barbagallo would take the dogs to a dog park.  
Councilor Vacon asked if the hours meant that the dogs would never be staying overnight.  
Councilor Purcell stated that was correct.  
Councilor Sullivan stated that was not correct.  
Councilor Purcell clarified that they would be staying overnight.  
Councilor Magrath-Smith further clarified that the hours meant that while dogs would be there overnight, 
dropoffs would not be prior to 7 a.m. and pickups would not be after 7 p.m. to ensure the neighborhood 
that people would not be going there too early or too late in the day.
9 
 
Councilor Purcell added that dogs would be inside the house at night and not outside barking.  
Councilor Devine stated that Mr. Barbagallo also explained that he would often be going to homes to pick 
up the dogs.  
--->  Report of Committee received and recommendation Adopted on a call of the roll of the yeas and 
nays--Yeas  10--Nays  1 (Greaney)--Absent  2 (I. Rivera, J. Rivera).

application for home occupation of Reynaldo Guzman for a barber shop at 113 Sargeant Street (010-02-
012) per 4.8.2. 
have considered the same and Recommended that the special permit be given a leave to withdraw 
without prejudice. 
Committee Members: 
     
Richard P. Purcell 
Michael Sullivan 
Mimi Panitch 
Nicole Maisonet 
Israel Rivera

send it back to committee.  
Councilor Purcell stated that there was an issue with the zoning and they were planning to send it back to

initiatives to help increase voter participation.  Voter turnout has been abysmal and we need to become 
more pro-active in a non partisan effort to improve that participation. 
--->  Received and referred to the Development and Governmental Relations Committee.

23. Thalheimer, Panitch -- Ordered, that the City Council (1) perform a comprehensive review of the 
Council Rules, in order to identify internal inconsistencies and redundancies, ambiguous provisions, 
archaic language, and areas where further information is necessary or desirable to construe said Rules; 
and (2) draft and adopt such amendments to the Rules as are found to be appropriate or necessary in 
light of said review.  This order is intended to allow the Council's committees to examine and recommend, 
and the Council to vote upon, technical corrections packages on an ongoing basis, rather than requiring 
the preparation of a single, comprehensive package of corrections or multiple single and specific orders 
for changes. In the event that the Law Department finds that more specificity is needed to conform to the 
Open Meetings Law, the makers of the order shall work with the Law Department to amend it to satisfy 
those additional requirements, and this Order shall be deemed to be so amended. Send to Charter and 
Rules.

discussion in committee.
